caption:
The robot that assists your operation now gets 8,192 practice runs, and the training takes two minutes.

NVIDIA released its Medical Physics Simulation framework as open source on 22 July. It models anatomy, device contact, friction and sensor input, so a medical robot can be pushed through thousands of variations of a body in software. The benchmark ran 8,192 robot-training environments in parallel and brought training down from over five hours to under two minutes.

What the robots learn from is the part worth sitting with. CMR Surgical contributed nearly 500 hours of anonymised clinical data from its Versius system to the Open-H Embodiment open dataset, feeding procedures including gallbladder removal, prostate removal, hernia repair and hysterectomy. The paper behind that dataset is blunt about why it had to exist: medical robotic datasets were small and rarely shared openly.

The caveat is plain in the announcement. Simulation comes before physical prototypes and lab testing, not instead of them.

Would you want to know whether the robot in your operation had done most of its learning in simulation?
